reader.requirement: At --std 85 a CLOSE naming several files (report files, and files of any organization and access) behaves as one CLOSE per file in written order, each with its own phrase, I-O status update and USE procedure, a failed one not preventing the later ones.

edition-consulted.switches: DialectBehavior.CloseWithLockLocksFileConnector: at 85 the physical file is locked, from 2002 the connector (the per-file close, not the series)

reader.edition-search: EmitClose's per-file loop (one implicit CLOSE per file-name, status store and USE hook inside it) has no edition test: grep DialectLevel/Edition/IsActive in SequentialIoEmitter.EmitClose found none; the EC-REPORT-NOT-TERMINATED raise is an EC-enablement question
reader.witnesses-cover: part: g85_bf18_09 covers order and per-file status for plain CLOSE; mixed phrases (WITH LOCK on one file), a failed close ahead of a locked one and a repeated file-name were not exercised (probed)

probes.printed: CLOSE FA PA WITH LOCK PB (FA never opened): USE-FA 42 PA=99 PB=99, AFTER 42 00 00, REOPEN-PA 38, REOPEN-PB 00; CLOSE PB WITH NO REWIND PB: TWICE 42
probes.expected: each file closed as by its own CLOSE in written order with its own phrase; a failed one does not stop the later ones; a repeated file gets 42 on its second close

citations.check: OK  §1985:XIII.4.2.4 GR7  (4.2.4 General Rules)  the text is in GR7

reader.notes: EmitClose emits one implicit CLOSE per (file, kind) in written order, each storing its own status and running its USE hook; the probe shows FA's failure handled before PA and PB close, PA locked (38 on reopen) and PB closed (00).

refuter.evidence: Read §1985:XIII.4.2.4 GR1-GR7 with table 1 (non-reel/unit CLOSE REEL: 'The file remains in the open mode') and SequentialIoEmitter.cs#EmitClose (one implicit CLOSE per (file, kind) in written order, status store and USE hook inside each; the EC-REPORT-NOT-TERMINATED arm is gated by ec.Enabled, not by the edition; grep DialectLevel/IsActive in the file finds no edition test in EmitClose). Probe r7close at --std 85: CLOSE PA REEL FR FI WITH LOCK PB over two report files, an unopened RELATIVE file with a USE procedure and an INDEXED file: PA=07 and still open (OPEN OUTPUT PA then 41, a second INITIATE/GENERATE writes ALPHA twice), FR's USE ran with 42 while PA was already 07 and FI/PB still 99, FI locked (reopen 38), PB closed (OPEN EXTEND 00, BETA kept). Each file got its own phrase, status and USE in written order; the failure did not stop the later ones. cite: OK  §1985:XIII.4.2.4 GR7  (4.2.4 General Rules)  the text is in GR7.
